findings.issue: Update step 4 says to merge the synthesizer's touched elements 'with merge.mjs --synth as in build step 5'. Build step 5 (SKILL.md:144) runs merge.mjs with --previous and no --areas, and merge() then treats every area as affected (scripts/merge.mjs:141, affected = null; isOwned returns true for every element). In an update the fragments directory holds only the affected areas' fragments (step 2), so every node, edge, entity and access row of the unaffected areas is classed as owned, removed, and not re-added. An unlocked element in an untouched area is silently deleted (a locked or noted node is kept with a conflict). The e2e test (e3) covers the --areas merge but not this synth re-merge, so nothing catches it.
findings.resolution: In SKILL.md update step 4, give the exact command: the same merge.mjs call as step 3 with --areas <a,b> and --synth <work>/synth.json added. Optionally make merge.mjs refuse, or print a conflict, when --previous is given without --areas and the fragments dir lacks a fragment for an area listed in previous meta.coverage. Add an e2e case for the update-time synth merge.

findings.issue: In update mode an area named in --areas that has no fragment in the directory (an explorer failed, a typo, or the new area for 'uncovered' files is left out of --areas, so its fragment is filtered out at line 147) is handled silently. Everything the area owned is removed (nodePart/edgePart/entityPart.gone), its coverage and sources rows are dropped, and nothing replaces them. Only authored nodes survive, with a conflict. The result still validates, so exit 0 and a smaller model. SKILL.md:221 says only '--areas <a,b>' and never says that uncovered-file areas must be listed too.
findings.resolution: Report a conflict (and exit 1 under --strict) for every --areas entry with no fragment, and for every fragment in the directory whose area is not in --areas. Say in SKILL.md update step 3 that --areas must list the areas of the uncovered-file fragments as well.

findings.issue: merge.mjs keeps its own globToRegExp, while P5.3 added scripts/lib/glob.mjs for the same meta.coverage globs. The two disagree: merge's version appends (?:/.*)?$, so a bare directory glob such as 'src/api' owns the subtree, while lib/glob.mjs matches only the literal path. Explorers write coverage globs by hand, so for such a glob merge.mjs replaces the area's elements while diffmap.mjs never reports the area as changed. The update flow then skips the area, or the two scripts disagree on who owns what.
findings.resolution: Import matchGlob/matchAny from lib/glob.mjs in merge.mjs and delete the local copy. If a bare directory should own its subtree, put that rule in lib/glob.mjs so both scripts share it, and add a glob test for it.

findings.issue: Model output is rebuilt from a fixed whitelist: meta keys (outMeta) and top-level keys (TOP_ORDER). Any other key in the --previous model is silently dropped on every merge, including unknown meta fields and unknown top-level arrays a newer schema might add. This conflicts with the additive-schema, readers-tolerate-unknown-keys rule (checklist 5) for a file users commit.
findings.resolution: Carry unknown top-level keys and unknown meta keys from --previous through unchanged, appended after the known ones in sorted order.
